newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore Power to up electricity rate 5.3 PCT.
newsitem.headline: Singapore Power to up electricity rate 5.3 PCT.

text.p: State-owned Singapore Power (SP) Pte Ltd said on Wednesday it was raising electricity tariffs because of higher fuel oil prices.
General tariffs will go up 0.75 Singapore cent, or 5.3 percent, per kilowatt/hour from November 1, a copy of the tariff change showed.
Fuel oil prices on the Singapore spot cash market hit a five-year high of $124.00 per tonne earlier in October. In June prices had stood at $84.
Prices have eased to around $118 per tonne by Wednesday but traders said they expect prices to remain steady in coming months.
SP last adjusted electricity tariffs in August when rates were cut by 2.0 percent to 14.22 from 13.94 cent per kilowatt.
The Singapore government plans to privatise SP and to raise SP's tariffs by 12-14 percent during the next two years.
